name: Today's Report
headline: Prop. 37, the new home loan measure, is projected to pass, and mortgage rates eased to 7.25% the morning after.
teaser: Prop. 37 (details at the top) is written for one kind of home: the loans go only to the first buyer, which in practice means new construction. In our five cities, 32 of the 570 homes on the market were built in 2025 or later, 20 of them townhomes, with a median list price of $1,128,500 and 14 priced under a million. They have waited a median 57 days, against 40 for the market as a whole. CalHFA still has to sell the bonds and open the program, so it is not available to buyers yet.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Prop. 37 (details at the top) is written for one kind of home: the loans go only to the first buyer, which in practice means new construction. In our five cities, 32 of the 570 homes on the market were built in 2025 or later, 20 of them townhomes, with a median list price of $1,128,500 and 14 priced under a million. They have waited a median 57 days, against 40 for the market as a whole. CalHFA still has to sell the bonds and open the program, so it is not available to buyers yet.

Rates eased the morning after. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.25% and the 15-year 6.86%, both down 0.05 from Tuesday. At 7.25%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,312,500 median with 20% down would pay about $7,163 a month in principal and interest.

The board wide table is 2,438, from 2,457 Tuesday, with 152 coming soon and 133 brand new. The five city ledger is 642, from 648: Fremont (218) and Newark (81) each dropped three, Hayward (182) one, Milpitas (100) added one and Union City (61) held.

What this means for you: if new construction is on your list, ask builders now how they plan to work with Prop. 37 once it opens. It is a loan that gets repaid, not a grant, so read its terms like a second mortgage's. Resale sellers compete with those builders, and 177 homes in our five cities have been sitting 60 days or longer, so price to this market, not last spring's.

  • Board wide: 2,438 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 152 coming soon and 133 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 642 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 570 are on the market and 72 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 218 live, 164 active, 34 coming soon, 19 brand new and 1 back on the market. The median on market list price is $1,312,500 at $823 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 37 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 182, Milpitas 100, Newark 81, Union City 61.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,049,975 at $666 a square foot. 276 homes are priced under a million, and 177 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Gas set an Election Day record (chart). EIA's survey put the U.S. average for regular at $4.15 a gallon in Election Day week, the highest for any Election Day in its records back to 1990, and San Francisco's $5.70 is its own Election Day high. Both were down from the week before, the U.S. by 12 cents and San Francisco by 16, and after inflation 2012's $3.49 would be about $5.11 today. A record in dollars, then, not in buying power.

Oil is sliding hard: Brent is down 9.03% this morning near $94.24, after settling Tuesday at $103.60, extending a slide that began Monday on hopes for U.S. and Iran talks. Metals are jumping instead, with gold up 3.39% near $4,073.90 and silver up 5.06% near $52.27. One correction: Market Briefs stamped gold at $3,948 (+0.20%) and Brent at $103.29 (-0.29%) as Tuesday's 4 PM ET levels. Both were Wednesday's overnight prices measured against Tuesday's settlements, a third day running, and Treasury has the 10-Year closing Tuesday at 4.95%, up 0.04, not 4.90% and down.

images.alt: Paired bar chart of the price of a gallon of regular gasoline in Election Day week, U.S. average and San Francisco: 2016 $2.23 and $2.78, 2018 $2.75 and $3.71, 2020 $2.11 and $3.18, 2022 $3.80 and $5.26, 2024 $3.07 and $4.42, 2026 $4.15 and $5.70, not adjusted for inflation
images.caption: Election Day week gas hit $4.15 nationally and $5.70 in San Francisco, the highest in EIA's records for an Election Day, before adjusting for inflation.
images.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, weekly retail gasoline prices; BLS CPI-U for the inflation note

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Stocks are rallying the morning after Election Day. As of 9:30 AM PT the Dow is up 2.87%, the S&P 500 up 1.78% and the Nasdaq up 2.03%. Tuesday was quieter: the S&P 500 rose 0.36% and the Nasdaq 0.83% while the Dow slipped 0.38%.

Santa Clara's AMD reported after Tuesday's close, and its data center business nearly doubled (chart). Data center sales were $8.5 billion, up 97% from a year earlier and 27% from the quarter before, and now make up 64% of the company's $13.4 billion in revenue. AMD expects about $17 billion in total revenue this quarter, up 66% from a year ago. The stock is up 0.57% this morning, still about 25% below its Oct. 6 high; the good news was not a secret.

images.alt: Bar chart of AMD data center segment revenue by quarter: $4.3 billion in Q3 2025, $5.4 billion in Q4 2025, $5.8 billion in Q1 2026, $6.7 billion in Q2 2026 and $8.5 billion in Q3 2026, up 97% from a year earlier, up 27% from the prior quarter, and 64% of AMD's $13.4 billion in sales
images.caption: AMD's data center sales rose to $8.5 billion in the September quarter, up 97% from a year earlier and now 64% of the company's revenue.
images.source: AMD quarterly earnings releases (SEC 8-K, Exhibit 99.1), through Nov. 3, 2026

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html: Bitcoin is back above $80,000 for the first time since Oct. 29: it is up 3.59% over 24 hours near $80,384, Ether is up 5.74% near $2,426.41 and XRP is up 2.23%, live from CoinGecko at 9:30 AM PT. Stocks, gold and crypto are all rising together this morning while oil falls, which is about as tidy as a Wednesday gets.
